name: The example
why: [[3, 7], [2, 3, 4]]. Lines 3 (2–3) and 7 (4–6) are bridges. Stations 2, 3 and 4 are cut stations: closing any of them splits the network.

name: Two lines between the same stations
why: [[7], [2, 3, 4]]. With a second line between 2 and 3, neither line is a bridge. Skip only the line you came along (by its position), not every line back to the parent station. Stations 2 and 3 are still cut stations: closing a station closes all its lines.

name: One line
why: [[0], []]. The line is a bridge. Neither station is a cut station: closing one leaves the other on its own, still one part.

name: A star
why: [[0, 1, 2, 3], [0]]. The search starts at 0, which has four children in the search tree: the start is a cut station exactly when it has two or more children.

name: Start with one child
why: [[0, 1], [1]]. Station 0 starts the search and has one child, so it is not a cut station, even though low[1] ≥ disc[0].

name: A ring
why: [[], []]: every line is on a loop, and closing any one station leaves a path.

name: Two parts, a loop line, a lone station
why: [[4], []]. A line from 3 to itself is never a bridge. Station 5 has no lines. The network has three parts to begin with; a bridge or cut station is one that makes more parts.

name: Two triangles sharing a station
why: [[], [2]]. No line is a bridge, but closing station 2 splits the network: a cut station need not touch a bridge.

name: A path of 100,000
why: [99999 bridges, their check number, 99998 cut stations, their check number]. Every line is a bridge and every station but the two ends is a cut station. The search goes 100,000 levels deep: a recursive version fails here.

name: 100,000 random lines
why: A sparse random network has many trees hanging off its loops, so many bridges and cut stations. Removing each line and counting parts again is O(E · (V + E)); one search is O(V + E).

name: A ring with a double line
show: a ring 0 – 1 – … – 99998 – 0, and two lines between 0 and 99999
why: [0, 0, 1, 0]: no bridges, and one cut station, 0. Station 99999 hangs off 0 by two lines, so neither line is a bridge. But closing station 0 cuts 99999 off, and the search from 0 has two children: the ring, and 99999. The ring is 99,999 levels deep.
